testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What can a trailer brake hand valve be used for on an equipped truck?

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve stops the truck from rolling backward when you start moving from a complete stop.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between the tires and the road
The time it takes for brakes to work

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between the tires and the road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road surface. Good traction is needed for braking and steering.

questions.question: What should you pay extra attention to during a pre-trip inspection in winter?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: In winter, check the coolant and antifreeze levels, defrosting and heating equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer fluid, tires, tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, handholds, steps, deck plates, radiator shutters, and exhaust system.

questions.question: How many driver's licenses can a person have?

options.text: Two: one for cars and one for trucks.
One for each state where you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only one.
questions.explanation: You can have only one driver's license. Having more than one is illegal and can result in jail time and fines up to $5,000.

questions.question: What should you do if you plan to stop on the road to unload cargo?

options.text: Stop suddenly since you are already on the road.
Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
Wave your arm out the window to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your brake lights to warn other drivers when you plan to slow down or stop where they may not expect it. Use this when stopping on the road to unload cargo or passengers.

questions.question: How should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Stare at the mirror for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look quickly at the mirror.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors with quick glances. Staring at a mirror for too long means you are not watching the road ahead.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, what should a CMV operator do?

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Not worry about speed and focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not know that your CMV must turn slowly. Brake early and slow gradually to give them warning.

questions.question: What is an acceptable oil pressure when an engine is running?
questions.correctAnswerText: 50 psi
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should be between 35 and 75 psi. Do not operate a vehicle if oil pressure is low, dropping, or fluctuating.

questions.question: Which direction do drivers usually look when turning?

options.text: In the direction of the turn
Opposite to the direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: Drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. Even without a turn signal, a driver's body movements can show they plan to turn.

questions.question: What condition should brake linings be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose, soaked with oil or grease, or dangerously thin.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before driving:

options.text: You should not see any part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
You should see part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should see part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. Seeing your own vehicle in the mirrors helps you judge the position of other objects on the road.

questions.question: When you start the engine, the coolant temperature should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually increase toward its normal operating range.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's aggressive behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what you saw about the aggressive driving.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while shifting gears:

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long while shifting can make it hard to move into the next gear. If this happens, do not force the shift. Instead, return to neutral, release the clutch, match the engine speed to the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, you must check for emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal.
The distance you travel from when a hazard appears until you see it.
The distance you travel from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is made up of perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels between the moment you decide to brake and the moment you actually press the brake pedal.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
Estimate the weight of cargo on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your wheels from locking up.
Stop your vehicle from speeding up on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: If you must drive very slowly and block other drivers, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and slow down traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: Most of the cargo is in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck is loaded correctly.
questions.explanation: Proper loading is essential for safe vehicle operation. Bad loading affects how the vehicle handles and can damage it. Improperly loaded cargo can also fall off and injure or kill someone.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. If you have a trailer, it must be straight so you can check your mirrors correctly.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle at the end of every trip, day, or shift. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staying within your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include: difficulty focusing, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits or signs, trouble holding your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting a shoulder rumble strip, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: When checking your windshield before driving, which is NOT necessary?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check your windshield for cracks or damage that block your view. Check the wiper arms have proper tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and that they are secure.

questions.question: If your driving test route has no railroad crossing, what will happen?

options.text: You won't need to do anything about crossings.
The examiner may ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route doesn't include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a simulated location.

questions.question: When driving a new vehicle, when should you learn the controls?

options.text: If you feel like you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Learn about a new vehicle's features and controls before you drive it.

questions.question: When should you slow down and be extra careful?
questions.correctAnswerText: When approaching a work zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in work zones, where the road edge drops off sharply, when objects are on the road, and on freeway on- and off-ramps.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you may need to:

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Swerve your vehicle out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve your vehicle out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you don't have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the company about problems that need fixing.
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly.
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the company about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the company of any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: What is the safest speed in heavy traffic?

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, a complete stop will:

options.text: Take a short amount of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle will need more distance to stop. This is especially true when carrying a heavy load.

questions.question: If you see taillights ahead while driving in fog:

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can assume the vehicle is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable way to find the road. A vehicle with lights on may have actually pulled off the roadway.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
Is not a concern for drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets the maximum weight allowed on axles. Axles that are close together have lower maximum weight limits.

questions.question: Headache racks:
questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo.
questions.explanation: A headache rack is a barrier at the front of the truck bed. It protects the driver if cargo shifts forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:

options.text: Inspected only about once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for tightness.
questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear during your pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep per night does an adult need to stay alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Eight to nine
questions.explanation: Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep per night to stay alert. This is important for safe driving of a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: Watch for black ice:

options.text: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road surface through it. Watch for black ice when it is below freezing and the road appears wet.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, you should:

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Push in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and oil that build up in the air storage tanks. This buildup can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving, especially if your tank has a manual drain valve.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space, then back into it. Position your vehicle's rear close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: During the driving test, when told to make a turn, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, always check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive into an open field.
questions.explanation: If brakes fail going downhill, first look for an escape ramp. If none is available, steer to a safe area like an open field or a road that goes uphill or becomes flat.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This is especially important when turning, changing lanes, or merging.

questions.question: When parking, you should NOT use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if your brakes are hot after coming down a steep hill. Let them cool first to avoid damage.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Smoother steering
questions.explanation: Tire failure signs include a loud bang, heavy thumping, or vibration. Heavy steering or fishtailing means you should stop and check your tires.

questions.question: A driver can rely on front wheel braking to work:

options.text: Under all conditions, except for snow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well in all road conditions, even on ice. Front wheel skids are unlikely.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: You can send texts but not read them.
You can read texts but not send them.
You cannot send or read texts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot send or read texts.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is not allowed. This includes typing texts or reading them on a phone or device.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means the ABS:
questions.correctAnswerText: Is not working properly.
questions.explanation: An ABS warning light means something in the Anti-Lock Braking System is broken or not working correctly.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: On a downhill grade, brake until your speed drops 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.
